Lynn, an Essex County city on Massachusetts Bay, lies about 10 miles northeast of Boston. It borders Nahant, Swampscott, Salem, Peabody, Lynnfield, Saugus and Revere. The only land link to Revere is the General Edwards Bridge over the Pines River, which matters for commutes and showing schedules.

More than a quarter of the city is Lynn Woods Reservation, and two beaches, Lynn Beach and King's Beach, face Nahant Bay.

Lynn is divided into Central, West Lynn and East Lynn, and each breaks into smaller areas that people name by square or park.

  • Central: the downtown business district and Central Square.
  • West Lynn: Pine Hill, McDonough Square and Barry Park, Tower Hill and Austin Square along the Saugus River, The Commons, The Brickyard, Walnut Street and Lynnhurst, and Veteran's Village.
  • East Lynn: the Diamond District and Lynn Shore, Wyoma Square, The Highlands, The Fay Estates, Ward 1 along Lynnfield Street, Goldfish Pond, and The Meadow with Keaney Park.

A house near the water in the Diamond District sits in a different setting than a triple-decker near Central Square, and a cash buyer prices the two differently. Give the street and the nearest square when you describe your property.

Europeans settled Lynn in 1629, and the city made shoes until the last factory closed in 1981. Electrical manufacturing followed, and Thomson-Houston Electric merged with Edison Electric in 1892 to form General Electric. The jet engine plant has stayed ever since.

Fire reshaped downtown twice. An 1889 blaze destroyed 296 buildings, including 142 homes, and in 1981 a fire at former shoe factories on Broad and Washington Streets burned 17 downtown buildings. Estates and beach cottages lined the shoreline in the mid-1800s, and Lynn Shore Drive opened in 1910 and drew more building along the coast. Many of those structures sit in the National Register Diamond Historic District.

The takeaway is age. A Lynn house built over a century ago may carry old wiring, plaster and original systems, and that is when buyers who purchase as-is are most useful.

Lynn has cold, snowy winters and warm, humid summers, with long freeze and thaw seasons next to salt air. Roofs, gutters, chimneys, exterior paint and basement walls work harder here, and deferred upkeep shows up fast. A cash buyer who accepts a house as-is takes on that repair list, so you do not have to pay for it before the sale.

Lynn has no interstate highway. Route 1A, Route 107, Route 129 and Route 129A run through the city, and the nearest interstate is the combined I-95 and Route 128 in Lynnfield.

  • Lynn station on the MBTA Commuter Rail Newburyport/Rockport Line, with about 20 minute service to North Station.
  • MBTA ferry route F5 from Blossom Street Pier to downtown Boston.
  • Numerous MBTA bus routes to Boston and neighboring communities.
  • Boston Logan International Airport, about 5 miles south.

New apartment buildings are going up within a half mile of Lynn station, including a 259 unit building on Monroe Street and a 331 unit waterfront project on Carroll Parkway, so the blocks near the station are changing. Homes farther out, such as near Lynn Woods, rely more on cars, so buyers there care about parking and driveway space, and about winter access on hilly streets.

State fire officials require the local fire department to certify your alarms whenever a home is sold or transferred.

Once a closing date exists, call Lynn's fire department and ask about the inspection fee. Battery-powered smoke alarms older than 10 years must be replaced with alarms that have 10 year sealed batteries, are photoelectric and have a hush feature.

Under Chapter 64D, Section 1, the deed excise is two dollars for each five hundred dollars of consideration, or fraction of it, outside Barnstable County. Your contract and attorney will say who pays it.

Massachusetts has two title systems, recorded land and registered land, and about 80 to 90 percent of properties are recorded land. Real estate attorneys are a regular part of buying and selling, both by law and practice. Ask the city of Lynn, and your attorney, about any local permits tied to your house.

A cash sale in Lynn skips the buyer's mortgage, so there is no lender appraisal or loan approval to wait on. You still sign a purchase and sale agreement, clear title and close with a deed.

  1. You share the address, condition and your timeline.
  2. The buyer reviews the property and presents an offer.
  3. If you accept, an attorney handles the title work and the paperwork.
  4. The fire department certificate gets arranged as the contract provides.
  5. You close on the date you agreed on and receive the proceeds.

Listing brings its own load: showings, inspector repair requests and financing that can fall through. Cash does not suit every seller, and an offer may land below a retail listing price. Weigh that against carrying costs and time.

Once you accept, the attorney orders a title search that lists mortgages, liens and unpaid municipal charges, and each is paid off or released. The alarm inspection is booked, and the deed is prepared for recording. At closing you sign the deed and settlement statement, your lenders are paid from the proceeds, and the balance is yours.

Because no bank sits in the middle, the usual causes of delay are an old lien and an alarm check scheduled too late. Both are easy to handle if you start them the week the contract is signed. Ask the buyer to put the closing date and the alarm certificate responsibility in writing so nobody is guessing later.

Gather your most recent tax bill, any water or sewer balance, the mortgage payoff statement and receipts for major repairs. If tenants live in the house, bring the leases. If you inherited the property, the papers showing who has authority to sign matter most. Having these together lets a buyer give you a firm number sooner and keeps your attorney from chasing missing pages near the closing date.

faqs.q: Is Lynn a good place to sell a house quickly?
faqs.a: Lynn is a large, dense market with 101,253 residents at the 2020 census and rail, ferry and bus service to Boston. How fast a house sells depends on condition, price and location, and a cash offer can shorten the timeline because no mortgage approval is involved.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke detector certificate to sell in Lynn?
faqs.a: Yes. The local fire department must issue a compliance certificate on any sale or transfer. Call Lynn's department for the fee and to schedule.

faqs.q: What is the Massachusetts deed excise tax?
faqs.a: It is two dollars for each five hundred dollars of consideration or fraction of it, set by Chapter 64D, Section 1, with a lower rate in Barnstable County. Ask your attorney who pays it under your contract.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lynn house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer who purchases as-is accepts the house in its current condition, including repairs. You may still need the alarm certificate, and the contract should say who arranges it.

faqs.q: What if I inherited a house in Lynn?
faqs.a: You may need probate steps before you can sell, depending on how the property was held. Speak with a Massachusetts attorney or the probate court about authority to sell, then contact us about the house.
